events.reader:

events.reader_segment: A hands-on electronics owner who is tired of improvising tools across phones, laptops, consoles, and household devices
events.promise: The Pro Tech Toolkit is worth considering when the reader wants one organized setup that covers varied electronics work beyond removing screws, with documented long-term protection for the tools.
events.arc: Email 1 establishes a fit test based on repair breadth rather than declaring the kit right for everyone. Email 2 makes that breadth tangible through one concrete prying tool and use. Email 3 addresses the purchase-risk question with the listed price, Lifetime Guarantee, and tool-replacement policy.

emails.job: Help the reader decide whether the Pro Tech Toolkit's breadth fits the range and depth of repair work they expect to take on.
emails.single_idea: The Pro Tech Toolkit is the stronger fit when the reader expects to work across electronics, game consoles, drones, RC cars, or vintage devices and wants opening, gripping, prying, and anti-static tools alongside a 64-bit driver set.
emails.objection: I cannot tell whether I need a broad 64-bit toolkit with extra opening tools or would be overbuying for the repairs I plan to attempt.
must_not_say: Do not claim the kit fits every device, model, or repair.
Do not present 64 bits as proof that every required fastener is covered.
Do not say the reader already owns inadequate tools or has previously stalled a repair.
Do not discuss the price, guarantee, replacement policy, Jimmy, discounts, shipping deadlines, or guaranteed outcomes.
emails.felt_need: I want a first toolkit broad enough for different electronics and for the stages that begin after the screws come out.
emails.mechanism: The kit combines 64 bits with an assortment of tweezers, spudgers, opening tools, and anti-static accessories; iFixit's stated device range includes electronics, game consoles, drones, RC cars, and vintage devices.
emails.call_to_action: Review the Pro Tech Toolkit's 64-bit set, repair-tool assortment, and stated device range on the product page: https://www.ifixit.com/products/pro-tech-toolkit
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the kit's breadth matches the devices and repair stages the reader wants one toolkit to cover.
emails.next_step_value: The product page lets the reader inspect the 64-bit configuration, the assortment beyond the driver, and the types of devices the kit is intended to support.
emails.next_step_limit: The page-level range does not establish that every exact model or repair needs only this kit; the relevant repair guide and any separately required tools still need checking.

emails.job: Show one concrete reason a general electronics toolkit needs more than screwdriver bits.
emails.single_idea: When a repair reaches a prying step, the included Jimmy provides a flexible steel blade and ergonomic handle intended for precise, powerful prying.
emails.objection: I already understand screwdrivers; I am not yet convinced the extra tools add useful repair capability.
must_not_say: Do not claim Jimmy is appropriate for every device, material, or opening step.
Do not promise scratch-free, damage-free, or successful opening.
Do not invent a repair procedure or tell the reader where to insert the blade without a device-specific guide.
Do not broaden the email into a list of every included tool.
Do not discuss price, guarantee, shipping, discounts, or deadlines.
emails.felt_need: Removing the screws is only one stage; opening the device may call for a tool made for prying.
emails.mechanism: Jimmy's flexible steel blade supplies the prying edge, while its ergonomic handle supports controlled handling; it is included in the Pro Tech Toolkit.
emails.call_to_action: See Jimmy and the other tools included in the Pro Tech Toolkit on the product page: https://www.ifixit.com/products/pro-tech-toolkit
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether a dedicated prying tool makes the full toolkit more useful than buying only a driver set.
emails.next_step_value: The product page shows that Jimmy is included and describes its flexible steel blade, ergonomic handle, and intended prying use.
emails.next_step_limit: This overview does not determine whether Jimmy is the correct tool or technique for a particular device; the device-specific repair guide still governs the repair step.

emails.job: Resolve the supported concern that a $79.95 toolkit may not remain a protected purchase beyond the first few repairs.
emails.single_idea: The Pro Tech Toolkit is listed at $79.95 and carries a Lifetime Guarantee; iFixit states that if an iFixit tool breaks, it will replace it.
emails.objection: I do not want a $79.95 tool purchase that becomes a loss if a tool breaks after only a few repairs.
must_not_say: Do not invent a discount, sale, deadline, scarcity, or cart activity.
Do not claim the guarantee covers the reader's device, repair outcome, consumables, misuse, or every form of damage.
Do not describe the toolkit as paying for itself or guaranteeing savings.
Do not reuse the device-range, 64-bit fit-test, or Jimmy arguments.
Do not promise a successful or damage-free repair.
emails.felt_need: If I spend $79.95 on my first general toolkit, I want to know what protection applies if a tool breaks later.
emails.mechanism: The purchase is backed by the toolkit's Lifetime Guarantee and iFixit's stated policy of replacing an iFixit tool if it breaks.
emails.call_to_action: Check the Pro Tech Toolkit's listed price and Lifetime Guarantee on the product page: https://www.ifixit.com/products/pro-tech-toolkit
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the documented tool protection makes the $79.95 purchase acceptable for a first general repair toolkit.
emails.next_step_value: The product page presents the toolkit's $79.95 price and Lifetime Guarantee, allowing the reader to evaluate cost and protection together.
emails.next_step_limit: The guarantee does not establish compatibility with a particular repair, protect the device from user-caused damage, or guarantee a successful repair outcome.
